boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Five Forks record (April 1, 1865) in the Appomattox Campaign [March-April 1865]. Dinwiddie Court House (VA086) precedes it; the April 2 assault (VA089) and Sutherland's Station (VA090) follow. Army-wide returns, campaign-wide loss and prisoner totals, the April 9 paroles and the retreat as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'Corps' and the live field zero. Sheridan gives the effective force of his three cavalry divisions on reporting on March 27 as 9,000 (Merritt 5,700, Crook 3,300) and Mackenzie's division as about 1,000 effective men; Humphreys says Crawford's and Griffin's were the largest and Ayres's the smallest of the Fifth Corps divisions, and gives Pickett's five brigades about 6,600 enlisted men on the February 20 return.
claims.rationale: Figures on different dates and bases (Union campaign-opening effective cavalry; a Confederate February return by formation); Crook's division was not seriously engaged. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Sheridan says Warren did not exert himself to bring up his corps and that portions of his line gave way for want of confidence, and that he relieved him under authority sent unsolicited before the battle; Humphreys prints the Court of Inquiry's opinion that there was no unnecessary delay and that Warren took the usual methods to prevent it, says Sheridan rode with Ayres and Warren led Crawford's line across the Gilliam field with the corps flag, and judges it a grave mistake to require Pickett to fight at Five Forks. The frozen commanders are Pickett (CS) and Sheridan (US), as on the live page; NPS says Sheridan personally directed the attack.
claims.rationale: Sheridan's accusations and the court's opinion conflict and are attributed, not adjudicated; Humphreys' judgment of Pickett's position is his own. Warren is not a frozen commander. No listed commander receives automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Sheridan reports the complete rout of the enemy and a pursuit of six miles; Humphreys calls Sheridan's success complete and says Anderson's troops were sent that night to cover the collection of Pickett's disorganized command.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The threat to the South Side Railroad and the evacuation of Petersburg are campaign consequences, not this record's result.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 3,780 (US 830; CS 2,950) and the live field 3,830 (US 830; CS 3,000). Sheridan reported on April 2 five guns and 'at least 5,000 prisoners', and on May 16 between 5,000 and 6,000 prisoners. Humphreys gives not less than 4,500 prisoners, 13 colors and 6 guns from the Fifth Corps and cavalry reports, Warren's 3,244 captured and 634 lost, and the Adjutant-General's prison records' 2,063 for Five Forks on April 1 (2,599 in all entries, including Dinwiddie Court House, Hatcher's Run and April 2); he did not find the cavalry's loss for this battle.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The prison-record entries include other places and April 2 and are not all this record's population.

open_questions: Warren's, Griffin's, Ayres's, Crawford's, Merritt's, Devin's, Custer's and Mackenzie's reports (Nos. 74, 75, 91, 97, 200, 201, 203, 260), Pickett's report, the Warren Court of Inquiry record beyond Humphreys' extracts, and the Union casualty return (No. 2) remain deferred. Fitzhugh Lee's report (selected; cited under VA086 and later records) gives Five Forks figures of 'over 26,000' against 7,000; it is not used here under the three-family ceiling. Sheridan's campaign-wide cavalry casualty list (inclosure No. 3, garbled columns) is not assigned to this record.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the commander of the Second Corps in this campaign, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; where it narrates his own corps it is a participant's account. It relies on the reports of Sheridan, Warren, Wright, Gibbon, Ewell and Fitzhugh Lee, on Confederate testimony before the Warren Court of Inquiry and on the returns, so it is not independent of those families. Lee's, Sheridan's, Bushrod Johnson's, Miles's, Gibbon's, Ewell's and Fitzhugh Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XLVI, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
